eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover and heavy rainfall forecast for Shanghai on August 10, linked to the passage of Typhoon Dolphin remnants, form the main driver keeping market odds tightly split between 28°C (44.5%) and 29°C (42.5%). Overcast skies sharply reduce incoming solar radiation while evaporative cooling from prolonged precipitation and moderate northeasterly winds further limit surface heating. Official guidance from regional models shows daily maxima clustered near 28–30°C under these conditions, well below the month’s typical 31–32°C average. Minor divergences among ensemble forecasts on exact rainfall timing and cloud thickness explain the narrow edge between the two leading outcomes, with only 10% probability assigned to 30°C or higher. Traders are closely watching the next model updates for any late shifts in steering flow or moisture.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from global ensembles and China Meteorological Administration guidance points to a daily maximum of 30–32°C for Qingdao on August 10, driven by lingering light rain and increased cloud cover that limits solar heating while sea breezes from the Yellow Sea moderate coastal temperatures. Historical August climatology shows mean highs near 28–29°C with a standard deviation of about 2.5°C, so values in this narrow range reflect typical late-summer variability rather than extremes. Model spread arises mainly from uncertainty in the precise timing and intensity of showers versus any brief clearing, which can shift peak readings by 1–2°C. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to 31°C and 32°C, consistent with the current ensemble distribution and the absence of strong high-pressure ridging that would favor higher readings.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service guidance and model consensus indicate Denver will likely see highs in the mid-90s on August 10 under a weakening upper-level ridge, with daytime heating tempered by increasing cloud cover and scattered thunderstorms associated with a passing cold front. Normal highs for the date are 89°F, but persistent warmth following the record 102°F reading on August 3 keeps temperatures well above average. Key variables separating the closely matched 94–95°F and 96–97°F outcomes include exact storm timing, which could reduce peak insolation by 1–3°F, versus clearer skies that allow fuller realization of forecast highs. Official observations from Denver International Airport will determine the daily maximum for market resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/zhengzhou/ZHCC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction models from sources like the China Meteorological Administration indicate Zhengzhou highs near 31–32°C on August 10, driven by weak high-pressure ridging with partial cloud cover and isolated showers that could cap peak insolation. These conditions create tight uncertainty between the leading market outcomes, as even modest increases in boundary-layer moisture or afternoon convection can shift the daily maximum by 1°C. Climatological August averages near 30–31°C provide a baseline, while ensemble spreads highlight sensitivity to steering flow and localized heating. Updated short-range guidance and official observations expected later today will refine resolution probabilities ahead of market close.
